1 Two-Year Master Roadmap

From Grade 7 enrollment through end of Grade 8 — a complete timeline covering subject study, Think English, and Zhongkao preparation

Key Milestones Gantt Chart

2026.09 - 2026.11 · Grade 7 Fall, first half
Adjusting to middle school + Think Starter sprint
English: all 12 units of Think Starter (3-month intensive, 4–5 lessons per week); Math: rational numbers → polynomials → linear equations in one variable; Chinese: narrative reading + introduction to classical Chinese; build the three core habits of preview, review, and error notebook
2026.12 - 2027.01 · Grade 7 Fall, second half
Think 1 kickoff + end-of-term sprint
English: first half of Think 1 (U1–U6), 3 lessons per week at a slower pace; Math: consolidate introductory geometry; Chinese: end-of-term essay focus; read Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk (朝花夕拾)
2027.01 - 2027.02 · Winter break
Think 1 continues
English: Think 1 U7–U9, maintaining 3 lessons per week; Math: preview intersecting and parallel lines; read Journey to the West (西游记) and Rickshaw Boy (骆驼祥子); push vocabulary past 1,200+
2027.03 - 2027.06 · Grade 7 Spring
Deepen learning, finish Think 1
English: complete Think 1 U10–U12 + KET mock exam; Math: systems of linear equations → inequalities; Chinese: expository texts + classical poetry appreciation; History/Geography/Biology handled in class
2027.07 - 2027.08 · Summer break
Physics introduction + Think 2 launch
English: first half of Think 2 (U1–U6), 3 lessons per week; preview Grade 8 Physics (mechanical motion, sound); Math: preview congruent triangles; vocabulary 1,500+
2027.09 - 2028.01 · Grade 8 Fall
Physics entry + Math push + Think 2 deepening
English: Think 2 U7–U12, slow grammar hotspots (conditionals, passive voice) to 3 weeks per unit; Physics: sound, light, heat, mechanics; Math: congruent triangles → linear functions
2028.01 - 2028.02 · Winter break
Finish Think 2 + Zhongkao warm-up
English: complete all of Think 2, PET mock diagnostic; Math: consolidate linear functions + Pythagorean theorem; Physics: preview buoyancy and pressure; sample the last 3 years of Beijing Zhongkao papers
2028.03 - 2028.06 · Grade 8 Spring
PET prep + Zhongkao starting line
English: 8-week PET intensive, target pass/distinction; Math: data analysis + end-of-year review; Physics: buoyancy + simple machines; launch formal Grade 9 prep over summer

Think Progress Tracker

Starter Phase (A1) · Fast 3-month pass

Intensive phase4–5 hrs / week

  • Grammar: be verbs, simple present, present continuous, there is/are, can/can't, comparatives, simple past
  • Vocabulary: 12 themes — family, school, food, animals, holidays, transport, and more
  • Pace: one unit per week, 4–5 sessions of 45–60 minutes each
  • Strategy: Starter content is light — build ear and core vocabulary fast without deep extension

Level 1 Phase (A2) · 7 months, steady progress

Core phase3 hrs / week

  • Grammar: intro to present perfect, comparatives/superlatives, should/must, past continuous, future forms
  • Output: short writing and speaking; critical-thinking discussions
  • KET alignment: each unit's Think Exams section trains KET question types directly
  • Pace: 2–3 weeks per unit — time to digest; grammar spirals upward

Level 2 Phase (B1) · 8 months, deep breakthrough

Breakthrough phase3 hrs / week

  • Grammar: present perfect consolidation, passive voice, conditionals, relative clauses, reported speech
  • Output: 150+ word writing, structured speaking, PET question-type practice
  • Goal: PET-ready by end of Grade 8
  • Pace: 2–3 weeks per unit; slow hotspots (conditionals, passive voice) to 3 weeks

Weekly Teaching Rhythm Template

Starter (intensive phase)

Mon–Fri: 1 lesson daily (45 min)
Weekend: unit review + Workbook practice
Finish each unit in 1 week

Level 1 (stable phase)

Mon/Wed/Fri: 1 lesson every other day (1 hr)
Weekend: writing + Think Exams practice
Finish each unit in 2–3 weeks

Level 2 (breakthrough phase)

Mon/Wed/Fri: 1 lesson every other day (1 hr)
Weekend: grammar focus + PET past papers
2–3 weeks per unit; 3 weeks for hard units

4 Daily English Listening · Ear-Training Plan

Based on the Think Cambridge English system — 20 minutes of graded listening resources every day

Starter Phase · 20 minutes daily

  • ① Morning 10 min: Think unit audio (current unit) as background ear training
  • ② Evening 10 min: BBC 6 Minute English — ~6 minutes per episode, slow pace, A1-friendly
  • ③ Optional: Himalaya A2 English story albums — engaging plots, ~800 core words

Think 1 Phase · 20 minutes daily

  • ① Morning 10 min: BBC CBeebies Radio — UK children's channel, real-speed fairy tales
  • ② Evening 10 min: Wow in the World — kids' science podcast, builds academic listening
  • ③ Optional: Daily English Listening app middle-school section — leveled by difficulty, adjustable speed

Think 2 Phase · 20 minutes daily

  • ① Morning 10 min: The British English Podcast — British accent, B1 match
  • ② Evening 10 min: BBC Global News Podcast — advanced news listening
  • ③ Optional: PET listening past papers — learn exam format and pace

Agent daily listening task: Every morning at 7:00, automatically push that day's Think listening links (Cambridge official audio / BBC 6 Minute English / Himalaya stories), including 10 minutes of unit audio + 10 minutes of extension listening. The Agent generates a weekly listening log tracking completion and comprehension.

5 Smart Error Notebook System

Auto-sort errors, spaced review reminders, similar-question generation  |  📝 Open error logging tool →

Error logging workflow

  • ① Photo or describe: child photographs the mistake or sends a text description to the Agent
  • ② Auto-sort: Agent identifies subject → unit → knowledge point → error type
  • ③ Tag: calculation error / unclear concept / misread question / forgotten
  • ④ Save to error bank: archived by date, searchable anytime

Review schedule (Ebbinghaus)

  • Day 1: redo same-day errors
  • Day 3: first review
  • Day 7: second review + 1 similar question
  • Day 30: monthly error review
  • Before exams: full error-bank sprint

Agent automation capabilities

  • Daily reminder: 8:00 PM push for "Today's error review"
  • Similar questions: auto-generate 2–3 practice items from the error's knowledge point
  • Weekly report: Friday error analysis (top error types, weak knowledge points)
  • Monthly comparison: error count trends and accuracy changes

Agent error-notebook task: Every day at 8:00 PM, push "Today's error review" and remind the child to redo same-day mistakes. Every Friday at 8:00 PM, auto-generate a weekly error report — count, top error types, accuracy trends — plus next week's review priorities.

6 Daily Chinese Reading Check-in

Required curriculum classics + extension reading + classical poetry

Grade 7 required classics

  • Grade 7 Fall: Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk (朝花夕拾, Lu Xun), Journey to the West (西游记, Wu Cheng'en)
  • Grade 7 Spring: Rickshaw Boy (骆驼祥子, Lao She), Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea (海底两万里, Verne)
  • Extension picks: A New Account of Tales of the World (世说新语, selections), The Analects (论语, selections)

Grade 8 required classics

  • Grade 8 Fall: Red Star Over China (红星照耀中国, Edgar Snow), The Story of the Insects (昆虫记, Fabre)
  • Grade 8 Spring: Classic Essays (经典常谈, Zhu Ziqing), How the Steel Was Tempered (钢铁是怎样炼成的)
  • Extension picks: Guwen Guanzhi (古文观止, selections), Tang & Song poetry anthology

Reading check-in rules

  • 30 minutes daily: fixed reading time (bedtime recommended)
  • Check-in format: book title + page range + one-sentence summary
  • Weekend output: 100–200 word reflection every Sunday
  • Monthly goal: finish 1 required book + some extension reading

Agent reading check-in task: Every day at 9:00 PM, push a Chinese reading reminder. The child replies with title + pages + one-sentence summary; the Agent logs progress and updates a reading bar. Every Sunday evening, push a weekly reading summary; at the start of each month, generate a reading report.

8 Agent Automation Setup Guide

Three steps to configure all scheduled tasks for fully automated study support

1

Configure daily English listening (7:00 AM daily)

Create a scheduled task: every morning, push Think listening materials — current unit audio link + extension resources (BBC 6 Minute English / Himalaya stories). Deliver to parents to play for the child.

Task: Daily English Listening Push  |  Schedule: Daily 7:00 AM

2

Configure error notebook review (8:00 PM daily)

Create a scheduled task: every evening, push an "error review reminder." The child photographs or describes mistakes; the Agent sorts and files them. Push historical errors on the Ebbinghaus cycle (days 1 / 3 / 7 / 30).

Task: Daily Error Review  |  Schedule: Daily 8:00 PM

3

Configure Chinese reading check-in (9:00 PM daily)

Create a scheduled task: every evening at 9:00, push a reading check-in reminder. The child replies with check-in content; the Agent logs and tracks progress. Push a weekly reading summary every Sunday evening.

Task: Daily Chinese Reading Check-in  |  Schedule: Daily 9:00 PM

4

Auto-generate weekly report (Fridays 8:30 PM)

Create a scheduled task: every Friday evening, roll up the week's study data into a report — subject progress, listening check-ins, error analysis, reading progress, and next-week plan suggestions. Deliver to parents.

Task: Weekly Study Report  |  Schedule: Fridays 8:30 PM

5

Monthly review and plan adjustment (1st of month, 8:00 AM)

Create a scheduled task: at the start of each month, adjust the study plan from last month's data — more time on weak subjects, harder listening, updated reading list, next-month goals.

Task: Monthly Study Review  |  Schedule: 1st of month, 8:00 AM

9 Permanent Multi-Device Access

Open the dashboard on any device without local-file limitations

Option 1: GitHub Pages (recommended)

  • Free, unlimited bandwidth, global CDN
  • Steps: sign up for GitHub → create a repo → upload the study-hub folder → enable Pages
  • Result: permanent link at https://username.github.io/study-hub/
  • Works in any browser on phone, tablet, or computer

Option 2: Vercel / Netlify

  • Free, auto-deploy, often faster
  • Steps: sign up for Vercel → import GitHub repo → auto-deploy
  • Result: link at https://project-name.vercel.app
  • Custom domain supported (e.g. your own domain)

Option 3: Cloud drive sync

  • iCloud / OneDrive / Baidu Cloud synced folder
  • Steps: put the study-hub folder in your cloud sync directory
  • Result: all devices on the same account stay in sync
  • Downside: each device must open the file locally in a browser

Recommended approach: deploy the dashboard with GitHub Pages (Option 1) for a permanent HTTPS link. Bookmark it in WeChat — open on any device. Agent scheduled tasks run independently; they do not depend on the dashboard files.
